matched_finding.description: The manuscript explicitly states that the CREP minimum sample size for this replication was set at 120 participants 'to ensure adequate statistical power,' and claims all studies in the meta-analysis collected this minimum. However, Table 1 shows the Gordon College study had N = 80, which is 33% below the stated minimum and equal to the original study's sample size. This undermines the claim of adequate power and raises questions about why this study was included despite failing to meet pre-specified inclusion criteria.
matched_finding.quote: All studies in this meta-analysis received this approval by the CREP team, collected the minimum number of participants specified by the CREP (120 for the present study to ensure adequate statistical power), posted their raw dataset, and reported a summary of results.

matched_finding.description: The Discussion claims the findings 'provide some support for social compensation theory,' yet of the four hypothesized relationships predicted by social compensation theory (lower self-esteem predicting preference for Facebook over FTF for safety, advantages, expression, and connection), only two were consistently supported (safety and, partially, advantages). The other two (expression, connection) were not supported or reversed. The authors cannot selectively cite partial support for a theory while ignoring that half the predicted effects failed to replicate, especially when the connection finding was directionally opposite to the theoretical prediction in most replications.
matched_finding.quote: The present research also provides some support for social compensation theory (McKenna & Bargh, 2000; Wilson et al., 2012). This theory suggests that for those with lower self-esteem, the anxiety provoked by FTF interactions can be somewhat mitigated in online interactions.

ground_truth.original_snippet: We chose to use the restricted maximum likelihood (REML) model because it has been shown to exhibit less bias than the more commonly used DerSimonian and Laird (DL) model with small numbers of studies (Veroniki et al., 2016).
ground_truth.modified_snippet: We compared restricted maximum likelihood (REML) and DerSimonian and Laird (DL) models and selected REML as it produced more interpretable heterogeneity estimates for our data (Veroniki et al., 2016).
ground_truth.description: Changed principled REML selection (less bias with small k) to post-hoc model selection based on 'more interpretable' results — explicit analytic flexibility

matched_finding.description: The authors report comparing two meta-analytic estimation methods (REML and DerSimonian-Laird) and selecting REML because it 'produced more interpretable heterogeneity estimates for our data.' This is a post-hoc, results-driven model selection decision—the model was chosen based on which one yielded preferred outputs from the actual data, rather than on theoretical or pre-specified grounds. This constitutes an undisclosed researcher degree of freedom that could influence heterogeneity estimates and subsequently affect interpretation of between-study variability. No pre-registration of this choice is documented, and the DL results are not reported for comparison.
matched_finding.quote: We compared restricted maximum likelihood (REML) and DerSimonian and Laird (DL) models and selected REML as it produced more interpretable heterogeneity estimates for our data.

ground_truth.difficulty_rationale: Unknown missing data procedures acknowledged — must expect this transparency in multi-site studies
ground_truth.original_snippet: Contributors did not always post analysis scripts, so procedures to account for missing data are not known for all studies.
ground_truth.description: Deleted acknowledgment that missing data procedures are unknown for some studies — reader assumes uniform data handling when it actually varied

matched_finding.description: The manuscript acknowledges that not all replication teams documented their procedures for handling missing data, calculating composite scores, or applying data exclusions. These decisions can substantially affect regression coefficients and effect size estimates, particularly in small samples. Without knowing whether teams used listwise deletion, pairwise deletion, mean imputation, or other approaches, the meta-analytic pooling aggregates results computed under potentially different assumptions. This limits replicability of both the individual studies and the meta-analysis itself.
matched_finding.quote: not all studies posted analysis scripts or narratives to help us determine such things as missing data handling, composite score calculations, data exclusions, etc. Data were not always collected or stored consistently (e.g., race collected in some but not all studies; individual item-level data were not always stored).
